chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washa', who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who emancipates his slave while he is in good financial condition, then later becomes needy. Is it permissible for him to sell him? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, when he is in need of that.'

key_terms.يُدَبِّرُ: He emancipates (referring to the legal status of tadbir)

ai.seo_question: Can an owner sell a slave after emancipating him if he later becomes poor?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the legal status of 'tadbir' (emancipation upon death) as a conditional, revocable act rather than an immediate transfer of freedom. It establishes that the owner retains full proprietary rights to sell the slave if financial necessity arises, provided the emancipation condition has not yet been triggered by the owner's death. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the economic realities of slave ownership and the interim status of the muddabbar.
